  "implied_focus": "The dimensions of the customer restaurant experience that Yelp reviewers discuss (food, service, staff, ambiance) and their resulting recommendation stance",

    {"name": "food_quality_rating", "supports_focus": true, "rationale": "Captures the food facet of the dining experience, a core aspect reviewers discuss."},
    {"name": "service_issue_type", "supports_focus": true, "rationale": "Captures specific service-related problems, a distinct experiential facet."},
    {"name": "staff_attitude", "supports_focus": true, "rationale": "Captures the interpersonal/staff facet, complementary to service issues."},
    {"name": "ambiance_atmosphere_mention", "supports_focus": true, "rationale": "Captures the environmental/atmosphere facet of the experience."},
    {"name": "overall_recommendation_stance", "supports_focus": true, "rationale": "An outcome/summary facet reflecting the aggregate experience, naturally tied to the other aspects."}
  ],
  "focus_coherence": 0.95,
  "structure_quality": 0.9,
  "focus_actionability": 0.9,
  "rationale": "All five columns cohere tightly around a single, data-inferable focus: the aspects of the restaurant experience discussed in Yelp reviews. They decompose the experience into well-separated, non-redundant facets (food, service issues, staff attitude, ambiance) plus an overall recommendation outcome, at a useful categorical granularity with meaningful value distributions and 'not_present' handling for aspect coverage. This is a sound aspect-based decomposition rather than a scattered grab-bag or generic mechanical features (no token counts or bare sentiment). The implied focus is highly actionable: an analyst can quantify which aspects dominate, correlate aspect ratings with recommendation stance, and target operational improvements. Minor deduction on structure because staff_attitude and service_issue_type partially overlap conceptually, and recommendation_stance is more an outcome than an 'aspect', slightly mixing facet types."
}
